About two dozen do not, including every security-relevant one: `UPDATE users SET role = $1` (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:652, :703, :718), `UPDATE users SET disabled_at = NOW()` and the re-enable (:898, :935), the entire 2FA lifecycle (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:69, :153, :187; 2fa/disable/route.ts:57; 2fa/email-setup/route.ts:55, :122; 2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:110; 2fa/verify/route.ts:180), OAuth link and unlink (app/api/v3/account/oauth/[provider]/route.ts:143, :150; account/discord/route.ts:240), the privacy toggles (account/privacy/route.ts:45, account/share-privacy/route.ts:59, account/posture-digest/route.ts:48) and every `UPDATE users SET stripe_customer_id` (app/actions/stripe.ts:130, :401, :614, :759). The column is nonetheless surfaced to users as fact: the admin export_data handler selects it at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:1275 and the self-service GDPR export selects it at app/api/v3/data-request/route.ts:129-131, in both cases as the account's last-updated timestamp.
findings.impact: A user who exercises their right of access gets an updated_at that can be months stale, having missed their own 2FA enrolment, every role change, an account suspension and un-suspension, and every OAuth connection change. For an operator debugging "when did this account change", the column is misleading rather than merely absent, which is worse.
findings.recommendation: Add one trigger function and attach it to the tables that expose updated_at, rather than auditing two dozen call sites: `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_updated_at() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN NEW.updated_at = NOW(); RETURN NEW; END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;` then a `BEFORE UPDATE FOR EACH ROW` trigger on users, notification_preferences, discord_connections, github_connections, user_ai_configs, staff_activity and support_tickets. Add it to the boot block in instrumentation.ts guarded by CREATE OR REPLACE and DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS so it stays idempotent. While there, add NOT NULL to created_at and updated_at, which the newer tables already declare (compare :640 and :678 against :320).

findings.title: users.email UNIQUE is case-sensitive, so the one-account-per-address invariant is a convention repeated across eight call sites rather than a database guarantee
findings.description: `email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL` (instrumentation.ts:284) gives a case-sensitive unique index, so 'Alice@example.com' and 'alice@example.com' are two legal rows. Every read and write currently normalizes by hand: lib/database/db-utils.ts:40 (`[email.toLowerCase().trim()]`), lib/auth/auth.ts:287 for createUser, :355 and :387 for createOAuthUser, app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:155 before both the identity lookup and the collision check at :204, app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts:61-63 before storing an invite email, and app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:129 for the per-email rate-limit key. That convention currently holds everywhere I checked, so this is a latent gap rather than a live bug, but it is enforced only by every author remembering it. app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:202 inserts `invite.email` straight into users with no normalization of its own; it is correct today only because the admin route lowercased the value before storing the invite. Two paths look up by raw email without a visible lowercase in the same file: app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:254 (`SELECT unsubscribe_token FROM users WHERE email = $1`) and app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:543 (the broadcast segment filter `AND u.email = $1`).
findings.impact: If any future write path forgets the lowercase, the resulting row is invisible to getUserByEmail, so that account can never sign in with a password and a second account can be created for the same human without tripping the UNIQUE constraint. The failure is silent at write time and only surfaces later as "I can't log in" plus two accounts for one address, which is expensive to untangle once billing and scan history exist under both.
findings.recommendation: Replace the plain UNIQUE with a case-insensitive one in instrumentation.ts: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email_lower ON users(lower(email));` (it also replaces the redundant idx_users_email from schema-05), keeping the existing constraint until the new index is verified. That makes the invariant a database guarantee, and it is also the index that would serve a lookup rewritten as `WHERE lower(email) = $1`.

findings.title: Five bespoke admin loading skeletons are exported through the shared barrel and rendered nowhere, so every admin section falls back to the generic skeletons
findings.description: components/admin/shared/skeleton.tsx defines nine exports. Four are live: Skeleton (line 10), StatBarSkeleton (143), SettingsFieldsSkeleton (161) and DataTableSkeleton (184), used from components/admin/admin-skeleton.tsx:3, components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:209 and :329, components/admin/features/ai-chats-manager.tsx:165, components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:8 and components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:522. The other five are dead: UsersListSkeleton (line 17), AuditLogSkeleton (40), UserDetailSkeleton (63), StaffListSkeleton (96) and TeamsListSkeleton (120). Each was written to mirror the real shape of one admin section while it loads. The file is only reachable through the wildcard barrel components/admin/shared/index.ts:8 ('export * from "./skeleton"'), and no consumer of that barrel imports any of the five: the only occurrence of each of those five identifiers anywhere in the repo is its own declaration line. Dead range is lines 14-139, 126 lines.
findings.impact: The bespoke per-section loading states were built and never wired, so the admin panel shows generic bar/table placeholders that do not match the content that replaces them, producing more layout shift than the author intended. Nobody can tell from the file that these are unwired, because the barrel re-exports them with a wildcard.
findings.recommendation: Either delete lines 14-139 of components/admin/shared/skeleton.tsx (126 lines), or wire each one into its section's loading branch: UsersListSkeleton and UserDetailSkeleton in app/admin/page.tsx, AuditLogSkeleton in components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:329, StaffListSkeleton in components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx, TeamsListSkeleton in the teams tab. Pick one and do not leave both states.

findings.title: components/admin/types.responses.ts is the one fully orphaned source file in app/lib/components/hooks: 60 lines of response interfaces with zero importers
findings.description: I built the full import graph over app/ (314 files), lib/ (252), components/ (313) and hooks/ (1), resolving @/ and relative specifiers and following barrels, then walked it from every Next.js convention entry point (page/layout/route/error/loading/not-found/template/default/sitemap/robots/icon/opengraph-image, plus middleware.ts, instrumentation.ts, app/manifest.ts and app/actions/*). Exactly one file in those trees is unreachable and has no importer at all: components/admin/types.responses.ts. It declares ten exported interfaces (AdminUsersResponse, AdminAuditResponse, AdminStaffResponse, AdminTeamsResponse, AdminTeamDetailResponse, AdminUserDetailResponse, AdminBadgesResponse, AdminActionResponse, TeamRenameResponse, TeamDeleteResponse) and imports nine types from ./types. None of the ten names appears anywhere else in the repository, including tests. The only other references are inside graphify-out/, which is a gitignored analysis artifact. 60 lines.
findings.impact: The admin fetch call sites type their API responses ad hoc instead, so the one file that documents the admin API's response envelopes is guaranteed to drift from reality with nothing to catch it. A developer who does find and use it may adopt a shape the API no longer returns.
findings.recommendation: Either delete components/admin/types.responses.ts (60 lines), or adopt it: annotate the res.json() results in app/admin/page.tsx and components/admin/features/*.tsx with these interfaces so the file becomes load-bearing and drift becomes a type error.

findings.title: scripts/migrate/versions/_legacy-original.mjs is 871 lines of unreachable migration code whose only import resolves to a file that does not exist, so it crashes immediately if anyone runs it
findings.category: archived dead script with a broken import
findings.description: scripts/migrate/versions/_legacy-original.mjs is 871 lines, described by scripts/README.md:31 as 'Archived pre-refactor migrate.mjs'. Line 23-47 imports 22 named symbols (c, log, info, success, warn, error, banner, section, loadEnv, askYesNo, askDanger, getProjectMeta, createPool, connect, confirmIntro, requireDatabaseUrl, parseDbUrl, formatDbTarget, formatDbHost, buildConnectionString, chooseDatabase, ROOT) 'from "./_lib.mjs"'. Relative to scripts/migrate/versions/ that resolves to scripts/migrate/versions/_lib.mjs, which does not exist: the directory contains only 1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs, 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs, 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs, _legacy-original.mjs and _snippets.mjs. The real helper lives at scripts/_lib/_lib.mjs, two directories up. The migration runner never loads it: listVersionFiles at scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:633-636 filters out every filename starting with '_', and findVersionFile at :613-614 only resolves '<a>-to-<b>.mjs' names. Nothing else in the repo references it except that one README line. Nothing catches the broken import either, because eslint.config.mjs:32 ignores 'scripts/**' and tsconfig.json does not include .mjs at all. It is also unreachable by the runner: the only two ways a file in scripts/migrate/versions/ is loaded are findVersionFile (scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:609), which builds candidate paths as `${from}-to-${to}.mjs` / `${to}-to-${from}.mjs` from registry version names, and listVersionFiles (scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:633), which explicitly filters out every filename starting with an underscore. _legacy-original.mjs matches neither, and it has been dead since commit fb8a71de split the monolith. Verified during the merge: the file is 871 lines, scripts/migrate/versions/_lib.mjs does not exist, and the underscore filter is present as described.
findings.impact: An operator following the README to 'the archived original migrator' as a fallback during a failed migration gets ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND instead of a working script, at the worst possible moment. Meanwhile 872 lines of stale v1/v2 schema knowledge sit next to the live migration steps, where a maintainer can copy an outdated DDL fragment out of it. Separately, 871 lines of stale v1/v2 schema knowledge sit in the directory the runner loads version files from, with its own private getActualSchema and version comparisons, so it reads as authoritative to the next maintainer looking for real migration behaviour and is a plausible place for someone to apply a fix that can never run.
findings.recommendation: Delete scripts/migrate/versions/_legacy-original.mjs (872 lines) and the line describing it at scripts/README.md:31: git history is the archive. If it is genuinely wanted as a reference, at minimum fix line 47 to '../../_lib/_lib.mjs' and move it out of versions/ so it does not sit in the runner's scan directory.

findings.title: The extension ships an orphaned public barrel plus nine unused library exports, including the severity-threshold helper the service worker reimplements inline and the OS-theme watcher that would make 'system' theme live
findings.description: extension/src/lib/index.ts (13 lines) says it exists to keep 'the deep import paths out of the popup/options/background code', but nothing imports it: every consumer uses a deep path instead (extension/src/background/service-worker.ts:46 '../lib/auth', extension/src/options/options.ts:14 '../lib/auth', extension/src/popup/popup.ts:11 '../lib/auth', extension/src/lib/scan.ts:14 './auth', and so on). It is the only orphaned file in extension/src. Behind it, nine exported values have no reference anywhere in the repo other than their own declaration: extension/src/lib/format.ts isMoreSevere (18-20), meetsThreshold (22-30), summarizeCounts (83-91); extension/src/lib/theme.ts effectiveTheme (26-34), watchSystemTheme (41-50); extension/src/lib/categories.ts PROBES_BY_ID (204-212), severityLabel (214-227); extension/src/lib/auth.ts loadAuth (17-20); extension/src/lib/types.ts ALL_SEVERITIES (8-14). Two matter beyond tidiness. meetsThreshold implements the notification threshold rule ('off' | 'critical' | 'high' | 'medium' | 'all'), and extension/src/background/service-worker.ts:746-756 hand-rolls that exact rule again with its own rank map rather than calling it, so the two copies can drift. watchSystemTheme subscribes to prefers-color-scheme changes and its own doc comment says 'Use in popup/options startup to keep the UI in sync with the OS when the user has chosen system'; it is never called, so applyTheme (theme.ts:8) resolves 'system' once at open and the popup does not follow a live OS theme flip. Total: 13 + 21 + 30 + 23 + 4 + 7 = 98 lines.
findings.impact: The barrel's stated contract is false, so a new contributor either adds another deep import or, worse, starts importing from the barrel and creates a second import convention. The threshold duplicate is a live drift risk on a user-facing setting: a fix applied to meetsThreshold would never reach the notification path. The unused theme watcher means the 'system' theme setting is a one-shot read, not a subscription.
findings.recommendation: Delete extension/src/lib/index.ts (13 lines) since no consumer wants it, or convert every deep import in extension/src to go through it and keep it. Separately: have service-worker.ts:746-756 call meetsThreshold from extension/src/lib/format.ts instead of its inline rank map; call watchSystemTheme from popup and options startup so 'system' is live; then delete whatever of isMoreSevere, summarizeCounts, effectiveTheme, PROBES_BY_ID, severityLabel, loadAuth and ALL_SEVERITIES remains unused.

findings.title: The docs component library exports a purpose-built ParamTable and DocsStepCard that no docs page renders, while the API reference renders its parameters with inline markup instead
findings.description: components/docs/index.ts wildcard-exports fourteen modules. Two exported components have no consumer: ParamTable at components/docs/docs-table.tsx:91-164 (74 lines including its doc comment) and DocsStepCard at components/docs/docs-steps.tsx:47-79 (33 lines including its props interface). Neither identifier occurs anywhere in the repo outside its own declaration. ParamTable is the more pointed case: it takes EndpointParam[] (components/docs/docs-types.ts:24) and renders the Parameter/Type/Required/Default/Description table with a conditional Default column, and app/docs/api/page.tsx does supply that exact data, declaring pathParams or queryParams on thirteen endpoint objects (lines 83, 112, 275, 283, 436, 476, 500, 562, 597, 755, 780, 862, 898). Those endpoints are rendered at app/docs/api/page.tsx:1211-1212 by EndpointCard, which at components/docs/docs-endpoint-card.tsx:52-95 renders both param lists with its own hand-written markup rather than calling ParamTable. DocsStepCard is the card variant of DocsSteps (docs-steps.tsx:12), which is used; only the card form is dead. Total 107 lines.
findings.impact: Two rendering paths exist for the same API-reference data and only one is reachable, so a styling or accessibility fix applied to ParamTable never shows up on /docs/api. The docs barrel advertises components that cannot be dropped into any page and expected to match what the site already looks like.
findings.recommendation: Pick one: either delete ParamTable (components/docs/docs-table.tsx:91-164) and DocsStepCard (components/docs/docs-steps.tsx:47-79), 107 lines, or have components/docs/docs-endpoint-card.tsx:52-95 call ParamTable for pathParams and queryParams and delete its inline markup instead.

findings.title: A no-op ternary in the Discord OAuth callback collapses a state/session mismatch into the same error code as a forged state, so the replay case the HMAC binding exists to catch is invisible
findings.description: app/api/v3/auth/discord/callback/route.ts:83-88 reads: const reason = verified.reason === 'expired' ? 'discord_expired' : verified.reason === 'user-mismatch' ? 'discord_invalid_state' : 'discord_invalid_state'. Both arms of the second ternary are the string 'discord_invalid_state', so the 'user-mismatch' test on line 86 can never change the result and is dead. verifyDiscordState (lib/auth/discord-state.ts:75) returns four distinct reasons: 'malformed' (lines 79, 100, 109), 'bad-signature' (88, 91, 94), 'expired' (112, 121) and 'user-mismatch' (128). The user-mismatch branch is the one that fires when a validly signed state is presented by a different session than it was issued to, which is exactly the leaked-state-replay case the HMAC binding at line 81 was added to detect. It is reported to the user, and to anyone reading logs by error code, as an ordinary invalid state. This is a second instance of the class already filed as AUDIT-011#docs-06 (components/docs/docs-nav.ts:153, 'item.exact ? pathname === item.href : pathname === item.href'); I scanned every .ts/.tsx/.mjs file outside node_modules and tests for ternaries with textually identical arms and these two are the only ones in the tree.
findings.impact: A user whose Discord link attempt is rejected because the state belongs to a different session sees the same generic message as someone whose state was truncated by an email client, so support cannot tell a benign copy-paste from an attempted state replay. The code reads as though the two cases are distinguished, which is worse than not branching at all.
findings.recommendation: In app/api/v3/auth/discord/callback/route.ts:83-88, give the user-mismatch arm its own code, e.g. 'discord_state_session_mismatch', and add a matching message on the login page, or delete lines 86-87 and keep a flat expired/other split. Whichever is chosen, log verified.reason server-side at that point so the distinction survives even if the user-facing copy stays generic.

findings.title: Two more empty leftover directories beyond the one already filed, both from the removed admin bulk feature and a removed admin users test suite
findings.description: AUDIT-011#bulk-06 filed the empty app/api/v3/admin/bulk/. Sweeping the whole working tree for empty directories (excluding node_modules, .git, .next, coverage, graphify-out, marketing and .claude) turns up four, of which two are new: tests/app/api/v3/admin/bulk/, the test directory that mirrored the same removed admin bulk endpoint, and tests/components/admin/users/, which has no counterpart suite anywhere (components/admin/users/ still exists with user-detail-panel.tsx, and its only test lives at tests/components/admin/utils.test.ts). The fourth, scripts/storage/json/, is a runtime output directory that .gitignore covers at 'scripts/storage/' and should be left alone. Note that git does not track empty directories, so none of these appear in git ls-files and a fresh clone will not have them: they are working-tree residue from deleted files, which is also why they survived AUDIT-011's fix of the sibling directory.
findings.impact: Small but real: an empty tests/app/api/v3/admin/bulk/ next to a live tests/app/api/v3/admin/ makes it look as though bulk admin actions have route tests when they have none, and vitest's include glob 'tests/**/*.test.ts' silently collects nothing from them. Directory listings and editor file trees carry a feature that no longer exists.
findings.recommendation: Remove the directories tests/app/api/v3/admin/bulk/ and tests/components/admin/users/ from the working tree at the same time as app/api/v3/admin/bulk/ from AUDIT-011#bulk-06. Leave scripts/storage/json/ alone. Because git does not track empty directories this is a local cleanup with no commit, so it must be done on each checkout that has the residue.

findings.title: Nothing in scripts/ or cli/ gets any static analysis: eslint ignores both directories and tsconfig covers neither, which is why a broken import in an 872-line script went unnoticed
findings.description: eslint.config.mjs:22-36 sets ignores including 'scripts/**' and 'cli/**'. tsconfig.json includes only '**/*.ts', '**/*.tsx' and '**/*.d.ts' and excludes 'scripts/create-fresh-db/schemas/**' and 'cli/**', so the 51 .mjs files under scripts/ (13,161 lines per the brief's measurement of scripts/) are matched by neither: not by 'npm run lint' (CI, .github/workflows/ci.yml:39) and not by 'npx tsc --noEmit' (CI, ci.yml:63). The CLI does get its node:test suite run in CI (ci.yml:109-111) but no lint or typecheck. The practical consequence is dead-04: scripts/migrate/versions/_legacy-original.mjs:47 imports 22 symbols from './_lib.mjs', a path that does not resolve, and no gate in the repository notices. ESLint's default recommended set (reached here through eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals) carries no-unreachable, no-dupe-else-if, no-constant-condition and no-undef as errors, which is why app/, lib/ and components/ are clean of those classes: I found zero unreachable branches and zero duplicate else-if conditions there, and exactly two identical-arm ternaries (dead-07). scripts/ and cli/ have had no such sweep at any point. A second, smaller symptom in the same tree: scripts/migrate/_meta.mjs:82 exports META_TABLE_NAME (a re-export of the module-local META_TABLE) which nothing imports anywhere in the repo, the kind of thing an unused-export rule reports for free.
findings.impact: Migration and database-repair scripts are the code with the highest blast radius in this repository and the least checking. A typo'd import, an unreachable branch, or a reference to a renamed helper in scripts/migrate/ or scripts/db-repair*.mjs fails at runtime on an operator's populated database rather than in CI, which is the same failure mode that dead-04 is already sitting on.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'scripts/**' and 'cli/**' from the ignores array in eslint.config.mjs:22-36 and add a minimal flat-config block for them (languageOptions.globals node, sourceType module) so at least the recommended correctness rules run. Add 'npm run lint' coverage of .mjs by including it in the eslint invocation. Expect a first-run backlog of warnings: land the config with only the error-level correctness rules enabled if the style backlog is too large to fix in one pass.

findings.title: Five CODEOWNERS rules match no path in the repository, including both database-migration rules, and scripts/README.md calls a script a CI gate that no workflow runs
findings.description: .github/CODEOWNERS lists five path rules that cannot match anything in the current tree. Lines 17-19 name /app/api/v2/auth/, /app/api/v2/billing/ and /app/api/v2/webhooks/, but app/api/ contains only security-txt/, v3/ and version/: there is no v2. Lines 33-34 name /scripts/migrate.mjs and /scripts/create-fresh-db.mjs, both of which moved into subdirectories (scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs and scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs) and no longer exist at those paths. The header comment on those two calls them the 'Database migrations' owners. Separately, scripts/README.md:63 states 'The CI gate `node scripts/find-duplicate-ids.mjs` is also part of the pre-commit checklist'; no workflow under .github/workflows/ runs any script from scripts/ (the only references to scripts/ anywhere in .github/ are the two stale CODEOWNERS lines). Duplicate check ids are in fact gated, but by a vitest case at tests/lib/scanner/registry.test.ts:60 ('check IDs are unique across the registry'), not by that script.
findings.impact: Low, because the catch-all '* @dbcaa @RejectModders' on CODEOWNERS line 10 already assigns both owners to every file, so no review is actually skipped. What is lost is intent: the five specific rules were written to mark security-critical and migration paths, and a future change to line 10 (say, adding a third owner or narrowing the catch-all) would silently leave the migration runner and the auth/billing/webhook API with no explicit owner. The README's 'CI gate' wording will make someone believe a check exists where it does not.
findings.recommendation: In .github/CODEOWNERS replace lines 17-19 with /app/api/v3/auth/, /app/api/v3/billing/ and /app/api/v3/webhooks/, and lines 33-34 with /scripts/migrate/ and /scripts/create-fresh-db/. In scripts/README.md:63 either reword to 'pre-commit checklist (see AGENTS.md); duplicate ids are gated in CI by tests/lib/scanner/registry.test.ts', or add a step running node scripts/find-duplicate-ids.mjs to the lint job in .github/workflows/ci.yml so the sentence becomes true.

findings.title: The API boundary mixes snake_case and camelCase for the same field on the same resource, so GET /api/v3/domains returns created_at while POST returns createdAt, and the shared ScheduleItem type declares two field names the API never sends
findings.category: inconsistent naming at the API boundary
findings.description:
Some routes hand back database rows verbatim and some map them to camelCase, and a few do both in the same file.

app/api/v3/domains/route.ts is the clearest case. GET at :29-42 selects `id, domain, team_id, status, verification_method, created_at, verified_at, last_checked_at, last_check_error` and spreads the row, so the client receives snake_case. POST at :127-137 returns the same resource with `createdAt: row.created_at`. A third branch, the already-exists path at :103-115, returns neither. components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx has to bridge all three: its DomainItem interface at :34-50 mixes snake_case (team_id, verification_method, created_at, verified_at, last_checked_at, last_check_error) with camelCase (verificationRecordName, verificationRecordValue), and its optimistic insert at :147-150 writes `team_id: null, verification_method: "dns_txt", created_at: data.createdAt ?? new Date().toISOString()`, hand-translating the POST shape into the GET shape and inventing the fields POST does not send.

The schedules pair has already cost a visible bug. app/api/v3/schedules/route.ts:28 selects `last_run_at, next_run_at`, but components/profile/types.ts:185-186 declares ScheduleItem with `last_run` and `next_run`, names no endpoint returns. components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:121-132 works around it at runtime with a comment that states the problem: "The schedules API returns `next_run_at` / `last_run_at` ... but the shared ScheduleItem type ... declares `next_run` / `last_run`. Read both spellings so 'when does this run' isn't silently blank because of a mismatch in a type this component doesn't own." The fix is a `sch as unknown as Record<string, string | null | undefined>` cast that reads `record[which] ?? record[`${which}_at`]`, which defeats the type entirely.

The scale: 46 client-side files declare 491 snake_case interface fields (largest: components/admin/types.ts 97, components/admin/notifications/notifications-manager.tsx 63, components/profile/types.ts 37, components/teams/teams-types.ts 18). Against that, four routes do map: app/api/v3/history/[id]/route.ts returns `scannedAt: scan.scanned_at`, app/api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/shares/route.ts returns `userId: r.user_id`, app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts returns `sessionId: r.session_id`, app/api/v3/account/discord/route.ts returns `discordId`. So GET /api/v3/support-tickets returns raw `created_at` rows while its own sub-resource GET /api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/shares returns camelCase, to the same component.
findings.impact: A client cannot assume a casing and has to check per endpoint, which is why one component ships a runtime dual-read cast and another hand-builds a snake_case row from a camelCase response. The ScheduleItem type is actively lying: TypeScript accepts `sch.next_run` and it is always undefined, so the compiler cannot catch the bug the cast works around. Any renaming of a database column also becomes a breaking public API change on the routes that spread rows, because the column name is the wire format.
findings.recommendation: Do not attempt a repo-wide conversion. Fix the two provable cases: make POST /api/v3/domains return `created_at` like its own GET (app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:132) so components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:150 can drop the translation, and correct components/profile/types.ts:185-186 to `last_run_at` / `next_run_at` so the cast at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:126-132 can be deleted. Then write the rule down in app/docs/api (rows are returned as stored, snake_case, since that is what 491 declarations already assume) and convert the four camelCase-mapping routes to match, rather than converting the majority.

findings.title: GET /api/version still does its own GitHub release fetch even though lib/updater/github-release.ts was extracted specifically to stop it, and the two have already drifted on timeout, caching and the release-url key name
findings.description:
lib/updater/github-release.ts:1-8 states its purpose: "Kept separate so app/api/version/route.ts and the admin updater routes can share the same 'ask GitHub about a release' code instead of each doing its own fetch + JSON shape assumptions." It exports fetchLatestRelease(), whose githubJson() helper (:52-62) uses a 10 second timeout and `cache: "no-store"` with the comment "Never serve a stale cached release when the admin explicitly asked to check for or apply an update."

app/api/version/route.ts does not import it. It fetches VERSION_CHECK_URL itself at :11-16 with `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` and `next: { revalidate: 3600 }`, then re-implements toRelease's tag parsing at :34-38 (`tag_name.replace(/^v/, "")` and the `html_url || RELEASES_URL/tag/tagName` fallback). It does import the other extracted piece, compareVersions from lib/updater/version-compare.ts, which is what the admin route's own comment (app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts:22-24) points at when it says the two "never disagree".

They already differ on three axes: timeout 5,000 ms vs 10,000 ms; cache one-hour ISR revalidation vs no-store; and the output key `release_url` (app/api/version/route.ts:40, :52 and the no-op branch at :25) vs `releaseUrl` (app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts:56 and :70) for the same value. `release_url` is also the only snake_case key that route emits, next to camelCase-free flat fields.

/api/version is not internal: it is the public unauthenticated version endpoint the browser extension calls (extension/src/lib/api.ts:200, typed at extension/src/lib/types.ts:199) and it is documented in app/docs/api and lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md.
findings.impact: A self-hosted operator can see two different answers to "is there an update" depending on which surface they look at, because the public endpoint can serve an hour-stale GitHub response while the admin panel never caches. Any future change to how a release is parsed (pre-release filtering, draft handling, a tag-format change, a GitHub API version bump) is applied in lib/updater/github-release.ts and silently missed on the endpoint the extension and the docs point at. The extension only reads `current` today, so the naming split is not currently breaking it.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite app/api/version/route.ts's GET to call fetchLatestRelease() from lib/updater/github-release.ts and drop its inline fetch and tag parsing, keeping the route's own `next: { revalidate: 3600 }` behaviour by adding an optional cache mode argument to githubJson rather than a second fetch. Rename the response key to `releaseUrl` to match app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts, keeping `release_url` as a duplicate key for one release since it is a documented public field.

findings.title: The AI chat widget keeps private copies of the four renderers that components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx was created to own, so the file whose own comment asks to be kept in sync is not the one the live widget uses
findings.description:
components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx exists to be the shared renderer. Its header at :10-18 says so: "The exact react-markdown component overrides the live chat widget (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx) uses. Kept here ... so any renderer of a stored AI message produces identical output to the widget ... If chat-widget.tsx's copy of these ever changes, this is the one to keep in sync with it (or, better, the one it should import from)." MessageContent's own doc at :123-131 goes further: "This is the single rendering path meant to be shared by the live chat widget and the admin AI-chat viewer, so the two can never drift into two different-looking renderers."

chat-widget.tsx does not import any of it. It defines its own `mdComponents` at :202-283 (byte-identical to messageMarkdownComponents at message-content.tsx:19-96), its own `MarkdownContent` at :283-289, its own `ThinkBlock` at :317-329 (byte-identical to message-content.tsx:111-123), and its own segment renderer at :431-470 that calls parseSegments exactly as MessageContent does at :141-159. Both files independently `import ReactMarkdown from "react-markdown"` and `remarkGfm` (chat-widget.tsx:24-25, message-content.tsx:4-5).

The only consumer of message-content.tsx is app/admin/ai-chats/[id]/page.tsx:9. So the module that documents itself as the shared path is used by one admin page, and the widget it was extracted from still runs the copy.
findings.impact: The bodies are identical today, so nothing is currently wrong on screen. The cost is that the module's stated guarantee is false: a styling or safety change to the chat renderer (a link rel, a code-block escape, the think-tag parser) lands on one of the two and the admin viewer and the live widget diverge, which is precisely what the comment says cannot happen. It is also roughly 130 duplicated lines and a duplicated react-markdown + remark-gfm import graph in the widget that AUDIT-012#fe-02 already flags as 144 KB raw on every page.
findings.recommendation: Delete mdComponents, MarkdownContent and ThinkBlock from components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:202-329 and import messageMarkdownComponents, MarkdownContent and ThinkBlock from @/components/ai-chat/message-content. The widget's :431-470 renderer differs from MessageContent only in that it renders `displayContent` (the typewriter buffer) rather than `content`, so give MessageContent an optional `content` override and use it there too, then delete the fourth copy.

findings.title: Nineteen helper functions have exact duplicate bodies across the tree, including a dead exported formatBytes whose private replacement fixed a bug the export still has, and a CVSS vector parser duplicated under two names beside the module that owns the bands
findings.description:
I normalized every top-level function body in lib/, app/ and components/ (comments and whitespace stripped) and grouped identical ones over 120 characters. Thirty groups came back. The five in dup-01, dup-03, dup-05 and dup-11 are filed above. The rest, with the sites that should win:

formatBytes: components/admin/utils.ts:218 is exported and has zero callers, while components/admin/features/backup-manager.tsx:39 defines a private one that is the only one used. The dead export is also wrong: its `sizes` array stops at "GB", so a value of 1 TB or more indexes past the end and it returns "1 undefined". The private copy handles TB and rounds differently (0 decimals at or above 10). The better implementation is the one that is not exported.

parseCvssVector: lib/scanner/osv-check.ts:203 and lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts:685 are identical, each with its own CVSS_METRIC_VALUES table (osv-check.ts:185, software-inventory.ts:672). The score-to-severity band function is duplicated beside them under two different names, severityFromCvssScore (osv-check.ts:227) and severityFromScore (software-inventory.ts:707), so a grep for one does not find the other. Both hardcode the bands that lib/scanner/cvss.ts:307 already declares as the exported CVSS_SEVERITY_BAND, and both comments point at cvss.ts as the source. cvss.ts exports CvssMetrics, computeCvssBaseScore, formatCvssVector and the bands but no parser, which is why each caller wrote one.

escapeHtml: three identical copies, lib/email/email.ts:98, lib/support/ticket-notify.ts:10 (whose comment says "email.ts has its own private escaper; this mirrors it for the support paths") and components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts:19. All three escape the same five characters today.

formatTimestamp: four copies in one directory, components/admin/features/email-logs-manager.tsx:79 and error-logs-manager.tsx:36 (with seconds), backup-manager.tsx:51 and billing-overview-manager.tsx:81 (without), so the admin panel shows two different timestamp precisions.

Also: fnvHash duplicated at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:75 despite lib/scanner/_helpers.ts:13 owning it; isSameOrigin (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:373) duplicated as sameOrigin (lib/scanner/auth/login.ts:304); withDnsTimeout (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:66) and withTimeout (lib/scanner/checks/dns.ts:93); isOAuthAuthorizeEndpoint in lib/scanner/checks/api.ts:64 and lib/scanner/checks/host-validation.ts:78; pathnameOf in lib/scanner/checks/page-checks/links.ts:108 and mixed-content.ts:44; tableMissingResponse in app/api/v3/scan/remediation/route.ts:37 and remediation/bulk/route.ts:37; asTrimmedString in app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:23 and landing-contact/route.ts:15; appendLog in lib/backup/job-store.ts:103 and lib/updater/job-store.ts:117; getRetentionLabel in app/pricing/page.tsx:26 and components/modals/premium-upgrade-modal.tsx:102; GithubIcon in app/repos/page.tsx:85, components/repos/github-repo-picker-modal.tsx:25 and components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:22; Cell in components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17; three identical stats skeletons in components/assets/assets-skeleton.tsx:8, components/history/history-skeleton.tsx:8 and components/shares/shares-skeleton.tsx:8; and severityCounts in lib/reports/compliance-report.ts:49 and lib/reports/markdown-report.ts:45.
findings.impact: Each pair is a place a fix lands once. The CVSS one matters most because it drives the severity assigned to a real advisory: a parser correction or a band change applied to lib/scanner/osv-check.ts leaves lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts scoring the same vector differently, and the two are used in the same scan. The formatBytes pair is the shape in miniature: the exported helper is dead, buggy at 1 TB, and looks like the one to reuse. Nothing here is currently producing a wrong result except the two admin timestamp precisions and the dead formatBytes.
findings.recommendation: Take them in three passes. First the CVSS pair: add `parseCvssVector` and `severityFromCvssScore` (derived from CVSS_SEVERITY_BAND rather than a second if-chain) as exports of lib/scanner/cvss.ts and delete both copies plus both CVSS_METRIC_VALUES tables. Second the scanner helpers: move fnvHash's call site in lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:75 to lib/scanner/_helpers.ts, export isSameOrigin from lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts and delete lib/scanner/auth/login.ts:304, and merge the two withTimeout variants. Third the UI: delete the dead components/admin/utils.ts:218 formatBytes and export backup-manager's instead, put one formatTimestamp in components/admin/utils.ts with an optional seconds flag, and hoist GithubIcon, Cell and the stats skeleton into components/shared/. Leave the three escapeHtml copies unless one of them changes, since a server-only and a client module cannot share one without moving it.

findings.title: The admin email preview reimplements lib/email/email.ts's layout and has already drifted on four elements, so what an admin previews before a broadcast is not what recipients receive
findings.description:
components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts:1-15 says what it is: "Client-side stand-in for the real branded email layout (lib/email/email.ts's `layout()`, server-only) ... This mirrors that layout's header, card, and footer; keep the two in step when either changes." generateEmailPreviewHtml (:28-80) renders the srcDoc for the preview iframes in components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx:402 and components/admin/features/email-logs-manager.tsx:414.

The colour half of the mirroring did get consolidated: lib/config/brand.ts is the single palette and both lib/email/email.ts:19-47 (via its COLORS alias) and email-preview-html.ts:17 read it. The markup half has drifted in four ways against lib/email/email.ts's layout() at :106-179:

  1. Logo. layout() uses LOGO_URL, absolutised if relative (:110-113). The preview hardcodes `${appUrl}/favicon.svg` (:55), so a deployment that sets a custom LOGO_URL previews the wrong logo.
  2. Responsive rules. layout() ships a `@media (max-width: 600px)` block with `.vr-shell` and `.vr-card` padding overrides (:135-141) and puts those classes on the elements. The preview has neither, so the preview does not show the mobile rendering.
  3. Preferences button. layout() renders a "Manage email preferences" button whenever an unsubscribeToken is present (:117-129). The preview never renders it.
  4. Support line. layout()'s footer reads "...or reach the team at <SUPPORT_EMAIL>" (:167). The preview's footer stops at "Choose what we send you in your account settings." (:69).

The preview also drops the `<title>`, the `supported-color-schemes` meta and the `a { color }` rule that layout() sets.
findings.impact: An admin composing a broadcast in components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx sees a footer with no unsubscribe control and no support address, then sends a message that has both, and sees the wrong logo if the deployment configured one. The preview also cannot show whether the message survives a 375px viewport, which is where the real layout's media query matters. Low severity because nothing sent is wrong, only what the admin was shown before sending.
findings.recommendation: Export the layout as a pure function of its inputs from a module both sides can import, for example lib/email/layout.ts exporting `emailLayout({ content, appName, appUrl, logoSrc, supportEmail, unsubscribeUrl })` with no server-only imports, and have lib/email/email.ts's layout() and components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts both call it. If the server-only boundary makes that awkward, at minimum port the four differences into email-preview-html.ts and add a test that asserts the two produce the same footer and header markup for the same inputs.

findings.title: Suite hygiene baseline: zero committed .only/.skip/.todo, zero snapshots, zero live network hosts, and one assertion-free block in 4,494
findings.category: measured baseline for the quality review
findings.description: Measured by script over all 356 collected test files so a later audit does not have to redo it. 4,494 it/test blocks. Zero `it.only`, `describe.only`, `it.skip`, `describe.skip`, `it.todo`, `xit`, or `fdescribe` anywhere, so no part of the suite is silently disabled. Zero toMatchSnapshot / toMatchInlineSnapshot and no __snapshots__ directory, so there are no unreviewed snapshots. Zero real third-party hostnames in any test: every URL is example.com, .test, localhost, or a spec domain, and every fetch is stubbed, so the suite runs offline and never touches someone else's service. Zero tests with an assertion inside a catch block and zero bare `catch {}` inside a test body, so no failure is swallowed. Exactly one block has no assertion of any kind, tests/lib/scanner/registry.test.ts:293, and its own comment says it is "intentionally a weak smoke test"; the other apparent cases all assert by throwing an explicit Error with a useful message, which is fine. No suite mocks the module it is testing. On layering: 142 of the 157 route.ts files have a route suite, but 92 of those 142 replace both @/lib/database/db and the whole @/lib/auth module with fakes, while 28 use the stronger pattern of a fake next/headers cookie jar plus a behavioural pg fake so the real getSession runs (tests/app/api/v3/auth/trusted-devices/[id]/route.test.ts and tests/app/api/v3/auth/impersonation-stop/route.test.ts are the best examples of it).
findings.impact: No action needed. Recording it so the next audit spends its effort on tq-01 through tq-09 rather than re-measuring, and so the 28 route suites that use the behavioural-fake pattern are recognised as the house standard worth converging on.
findings.recommendation: When touching a route suite that currently mocks @/lib/auth wholesale, convert it to the tests/app/api/v3/auth/trusted-devices/[id]/route.test.ts pattern: a fake next/headers cookie jar plus a pg fake that answers by SQL prefix and captures params, so getSession and the ownership-scoped SQL both run for real.

findings.title: npm audit is clean, every package resolves from the public registry, and the lockfile's Linux native bindings are intact
findings.description: Recording the negative results so the next audit does not redo them. `npm audit --json` on the full tree reports 0 vulnerabilities across 813 packages (369 prod, 363 dev, 137 optional, 1 peer) at every severity including info, so there is no reachability analysis to do: nothing is reported. `npm view <pkg> deprecated` across all 86 direct dependencies returns nothing, and no lockfile entry carries a `deprecated` field. Scanning all 814 lockfile entries, every single `resolved` URL points at https://registry.npmjs.org: there are no git URLs, no tarball URLs, no alternate registries and no `file:` links. Two things here are worth an operator knowing: the lockfile is currently healthy on the exact axis that has broken this repo before, so whoever applies deps-01, deps-02 or deps-08 needs to regenerate it on Linux or graft entries by hand rather than running npm install on Windows; and `npm audit` being clean means the CI gate at ci.yml (`npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev`) is currently passing on merit rather than on a suppression.
findings.recommendation: No change. When applying any of the package.json edits in this section, re-run the Linux-binding check afterwards: the thirteen entries listed above must still be present in package-lock.json before the change is committed.

findings.title: Sixteen packages are behind, and only next and typescript are majors: both are deliberately held, and the rest are minor or patch drift with no security content
findings.description: `npm outdated --json` lists sixteen entries. Two are majors and both are held on purpose, documented in .github/dependabot.yml:73-81. (a) `next` 15.5.23 vs 16.3.3 (package.json:95), with `update-types: ["version-update:semver-major"]` ignored so the Next 16 jump arrives as a manual decision rather than an automated PR. Next 15.5.23 is well past the 15.2.3 that fixed the middleware-bypass advisory and npm audit reports nothing against it, so this is a planning item, not a security one, though see deps-13 for the eslint-config-next half of it having already moved. (b) `typescript` 6.0.3 vs 7.0.2 (package.json:135), held because `@typescript-eslint/*` 8.67.0 declares `typescript: ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0"`, so TS 7 would break both the lint and typecheck CI jobs; dependabot.yml:78-81 states exactly this. The other fourteen are minors and patches with no advisory content: @ai-sdk/anthropic and @ai-sdk/openai and `ai` (all unused, see deps-01), @types/node 26.2.0 vs 26.4.0, @types/react-dom, @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin and parser 8.67.0 vs 8.68.0, eslint-config-next 16.3.2 vs 16.3.3, lucide-react 1.34.0 vs 1.35.0, nodemailer 9.0.5 vs 9.0.6, stripe 22.5.0 vs 22.6.0, and zod 4.4.3 vs 4.5.2. Note that `npm outdated`'s `current` column here reflects a workspace whose node_modules has drifted below the lockfile in three places (eslint 10.8.1 installed against 10.9.0 locked, @ai-sdk/anthropic 4.0.40 against a `^4.0.41` floor, react-hook-form 7.85.0 against an exact 7.86.0 pin), which is a local-install artifact, not a repo state: `npm ci` on CI resolves the locked versions and the CI run on main is green.
findings.impact: None urgent. The one thing worth tracking is the typescript hold: it is correctly reasoned and correctly documented today, but it couples the TypeScript version the whole codebase compiles against to a single lint plugin's peer range, so it needs revisiting when typescript-eslint ships TS 7 support rather than being left to drift.
findings.recommendation: No action needed on the fourteen minors beyond letting dependabot's weekly PRs land. Add a dated note to the typescript ignore rule at .github/dependabot.yml:78-81 so the hold is revisited rather than becoming permanent, and treat the Next 16 upgrade as its own scheduled piece of work given deps-13 shows the lint half already moved ahead of it.

findings.title: .gitignore line 56 is a typo, `nscripts/storage/`, which matches no path and duplicates the correct `scripts/storage/` three lines below
findings.description: `.gitignore:56` contains `nscripts/storage/`, sitting at the end of the "Dependency directories" block after the four `.yarn/*` entries. There is no `nscripts` directory in the repo (`ls -d nscripts` returns nothing), so the pattern matches nothing. The intended pattern is present and correct three lines later at `.gitignore:59`, `scripts/storage/`, under its own "FP audit temporary scan storage" comment. The likely cause is a stray `n` from a keystroke landing at the start of a duplicated line. Note also that this is the only defect I found in gitignore coverage for the sub-projects: `git ls-files | grep node_modules` returns nothing, no `dist-chrome`, `dist-firefox` or `.zip` artifact is tracked, `extension/.gitignore` correctly covers `node_modules/`, `dist-chrome/`, `dist-firefox/`, `dist-build/`, `dist-tsc/`, `out/`, `*.tsbuildinfo` and `vulnradar-*.zip`, and the comment at `.gitignore:66` explaining why the root must not add `extension/*` is accurate.
findings.impact: None functionally. It is a misleading line in a file people read when deciding what is and is not committed, and it looks like `scripts/storage/` is ignored twice when one of the two is dead.
findings.recommendation: Delete `.gitignore:56`. The real pattern at line 59 already covers it.

findings.title: Rollback coverage is complete at the version level but the 11 boot-only tables have no down step, so a downgrade leaves them behind as orphans
findings.description: Answering the rollback question directly: every registered transition does have a down step. scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:573 composes transitions pairwise across the three registry versions, findVersionFile (line 609) resolves 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 to 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs (which exports `downgrade` at line 1169) and 2.0.0 to 1.0.0 to 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs, so there is no missing rollback path. The gap is the same one as migrate-01 seen from the other direction: because the 11 boot-only tables are created by no upgrade step, the downgrade's dropTables list (line 1204-1230) does not include them either, so a 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 downgrade leaves browserbase_credit_purchases, browserbase_usage, domains, email_logs, github_credit_purchases, scan_screenshots, support_tickets, support_ticket_messages, support_ticket_shares, user_avatars and worker_failure_state in place. All 11 have FKs to users or scan_history with ON DELETE CASCADE or SET NULL, so the downgrade's `DELETE FROM users WHERE password_hash IS NULL` (line 1293) does not error on them, and a subsequent 2.0.0 to 1.0.0 downgrade does not error either.
findings.impact: No failure and no data loss, but a downgraded database ends up as a mixture: it fingerprints as 2.0.0 (fingerprintDetect only requires the fingerprint's tables to be present, scripts/migrate/_detect.mjs:33) while carrying 11 v3.7-era tables full of live data that the v2 app cannot read and that nothing will clean up. Also worth recording that the destructive-step counter shown before an upgrade (migrate.mjs:479) is driven only by dropTable and dropColumn kinds, so on the 2.0.0 to 3.0.0 upgrade it reports exactly one destructive step (the year_month DROP COLUMN at line 1134) and the upgrade path therefore never prompts for anything meaningful.
findings.recommendation: Fold into migrate-01's fix: when the 11 tables are added to addTables, add the same names to dropTables in the downgrade, ordered so children (support_ticket_messages, support_ticket_shares) precede parents (support_tickets). The DROP TABLE ... CASCADE that _planner.mjs:92 already emits handles the rest.

findings.title: Column types are inconsistent for the same kind of value across tables: IP addresses in three different types, and two JSON payloads stored as TEXT
findings.description: The schema stores an IP address three different ways: `INET` in security_alerts.ip_address (instrumentation.ts:1100), `VARCHAR(45)` in sessions (:336), sessions.ipv4_address (:352), api_keys.bound_ip (:382), admin_audit_log (:574), device_trust (:856) and access_rules (implicitly, in the TEXT `value` column at :1009), and plain `TEXT` in staff_activity.ip_address (:736). Only the INET column can be compared with a subnet operator or validated by the database; the VARCHAR ones silently accept anything up to 45 characters, which matters for api_keys.bound_ip because lib/api/api-keys.ts's passesApiKeyIpBinding compares it as a string. Two JSON payloads are stored as TEXT while everything else in the schema uses JSONB: `users.backup_codes TEXT` (:316), which is written with JSON.stringify (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:110) and read with JSON.parse (:49), and which app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:156 probes with the string comparison `u.backup_codes IS NOT NULL AND u.backup_codes != '[]'` to compute has_backup_codes, so any serialization that emits `[ ]` or `null` instead of exactly `[]` flips that flag; and `data_requests.data TEXT` (:874), which holds the whole GDPR export document. Positives worth recording, since they are the things that usually go wrong: money is integer cents everywhere (billing_history.amount_cents INTEGER at :525, all three credit ledgers use BIGINT token counts), there is no float anywhere in the schema, and every timestamp is TIMESTAMPTZ or TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE with no naked `timestamp` column, so there is no time-zone ambiguity to fix.
findings.impact: No current failure. The cost is that a query cannot mix these columns (you cannot join or compare security_alerts.ip_address against sessions.ip_address without a cast), no CIDR or subnet analysis is possible over the VARCHAR ones, and the has_backup_codes flag in the admin user detail view depends on exact string equality with '[]' rather than on a structural check the database could do.
findings.recommendation: Low priority, but when any of these tables is next touched: migrate staff_activity.ip_address to VARCHAR(45) to match its six siblings (or migrate all seven to INET, which is the better target and lets the admin panel do subnet queries), and convert users.backup_codes and data_requests.data to JSONB so app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:156 can use `jsonb_array_length(backup_codes) > 0` instead of comparing text to '[]'. Both conversions are `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE jsonb USING col::jsonb`, safe on existing rows since both already contain valid JSON.

findings.title: There are no actionable TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers and no commented-out code blocks anywhere in the source: all 14 marker matches are scanner detection patterns or display placeholders
findings.category: verified clean: deferred-work markers and commented-out code
findings.description: Item 6 of the scope expected 14 TODO-family markers across app, lib, components, extension/src, cli and scripts. All 14 matches exist, and none is a deferred-work marker. Seven are the scanner's own detection logic, which looks for these strings in the sites it scans: lib/scanner/checks/content.ts:841 (comment naming the keyword set), :1899 (the regex /(?:TODO|FIXME|XXX|HACK|console\.log|debugger)/i) and :1902 (its finding message); lib/scanner/checks/information-disclosure.ts:456-457 (a comment recording that this keyword family was deliberately REMOVED from that check because it fires on nearly every real site); lib/scanner/checks/vibe-code.ts:91 and :93 (a regex for a TODO comment naming an unimplemented security control, and its message). The other seven are the literal string 'XXXX' used as a formatting placeholder or a fake key: lib/scanner/checks/content.ts:1641, lib/scanner/checks/secrets-extended.ts:24, lib/ai/verify-context.ts:93, app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts:122, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:31, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:18 and components/auth/login-2fa-form.tsx:143 (the backup-code input placeholder 'XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX'). Nothing in extension/src, cli/ or scripts/ matches at all. Separately, item 5: I scanned every .ts/.tsx/.mjs file outside node_modules for runs of three or more consecutive // lines whose content parses as code, and then for any single line matching ^\s*//\s*(const|let|var|import|export|return|await|function|class|if \(|for \(|console\.log). Both produced only prose. There is no commented-out code in this repository.
findings.impact: None: this is a clean result. It is recorded so a later audit does not spend the same effort re-deriving it, and so the 14 raw grep hits are not mistaken for a backlog. The one thing worth knowing is that a real TODO added to this codebase today would be the only one, so a lint rule that forbids them would pass immediately.
findings.recommendation: No action required. If the owner wants to keep it that way, add 'no-warning-comments' at warn level for terms TODO/FIXME/HACK to eslint.config.mjs, scoped to app/, lib/, components/ and hooks/, and exclude lib/scanner/checks/ where those strings are detection data rather than notes.

findings.title: A full Radix toast stack is mounted on every page for exactly one consumer while 50 components hand-roll their own error and success banner state
findings.category: two mechanisms for the same job
findings.description:
components/ui/use-toast.ts (191 lines), components/ui/toast.tsx and components/ui/toaster.tsx implement a Radix-backed toast queue, and app/layout.tsx:195 mounts <Toaster /> inside the root layout so it renders on every route. components/ui/toaster.tsx:13-18 records that this mounting was itself a fix: "Mounted once in app/layout.tsx: without it the toast state updated but nothing ever drew it, so every toast() call (e.g. the billing-verification modal's error/success feedback) was silent."

That billing-verification modal is still the only consumer. components/profile/modals/billing-verification-modal.tsx:138 is the single `useToast()` call site outside components/ui/ itself; it fires nine toasts. Every other surface in the app reports success and failure one of two other ways: a locally held `useState<string | null>(null)` banner pair (50 files) or a setError/setSuccess pair prop-drilled down from the page (the profile tab tree, typed at components/profile/types.ts and threaded through profile-social-tab.tsx, profile-notifications-tab.tsx and developer/domains-section.tsx). A third mechanism, the admin-authored site notification with `type: "toast"`, is rendered by components/shared/site-notifications.tsx and shares nothing with the Radix stack.
findings.impact: No user-visible bug: the modal's toasts work and the banners work. The cost is that feedback looks and behaves differently depending on which of three mechanisms a screen happened to use, that a Radix provider and its dependency ship on every page load for one modal, and that a new contributor picking a pattern has no signal about which one is intended. This is the reason a fix like "errors should auto-dismiss" or "errors should be announced to screen readers" cannot be made once.
findings.recommendation: Decide which one wins and write it in CLAUDE.md. If toasts win, migrate the 50 local-banner components in batches and delete the prop-drilled setError/setSuccess from components/profile/types.ts. If banners win, delete components/ui/toaster.tsx, components/ui/toast.tsx and components/ui/use-toast.ts, drop <Toaster /> from app/layout.tsx:195, and convert components/profile/modals/billing-verification-modal.tsx's nine calls to the banner pattern its parent already uses. Either way this is not urgent; it is worth deciding before the next batch of forms is written.

findings.title: Negative result for the next audit: the four config surfaces share no duplicated export, all 271 registry defaults derive from CONFIG_ constants, and all seven paginated routes use the same page/limit convention
findings.description:
I checked the specific split-brain shape AUDIT-009#dup-01 found (RATE_LIMITS defined in two places so 11 routes bypassed the admin-configured values) against the current tree and it has not recurred.

Extracting every `export const` and `export function` from lib/config/constants.ts (788 lines), lib/config/client-constants.ts (378), lib/config/config-values.ts (1,368), lib/config/registry.ts, lib/config/brand.ts and lib/config/env.ts gives zero names exported from more than one of them. The layering holds in the direction it is documented: config-values.ts holds the literals, constants.ts imports and re-exports them (RATE_LIMITS at constants.ts:360-470 is built entirely from CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_* imports, with no second literal anywhere), and client-constants.ts is re-exported through constants.ts rather than redefined.

lib/config/registry.ts contains 272 `default:` entries and every one of them is a CONFIG_ constant imported from config-values.ts, not a literal, so an admin-editable setting cannot fall back to a value that disagrees with the compiled one. The comment at registry.ts:1-11 describes that rule and the code follows it.

Separately, every paginated endpoint uses the same query convention: `page` and `limit` in all seven (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts, admin/content, admin/email-logs, admin/error-logs, admin/teams, ai/conversations, public-scans). Nothing uses offset or a cursor. The response-side key drift is filed as dup-08; the request side is consistent.

The brand palette is likewise consolidated: lib/config/brand.ts is the single source and lib/email/email.ts:19-47 aliases it rather than holding its own hexes, which is what the comment at brand.ts:1-13 claims.
findings.impact: None. Recorded so the next audit does not spend time re-deriving these four surfaces or re-checking pagination conventions.
findings.recommendation: No action. Keep the registry.ts:1-11 rule ("Adding a configurable value means adding an entry here, not a bare constant") enforced in review; it is the thing preventing the AUDIT-009 shape from returning.
